hero.lead: An island nation of 9.4 million in the Caribbean, with farmland across six tenths of its land, where Cuba is not a member of the IMF or the World Bank and no capital already committed is on record.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2023
items.text: Land that can feed the nation and earn abroad, valued and financed against its harvest.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Standing forest that stores carbon and water, and can earn as it stands.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, end of 2025
items.text: 15% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: The Land
items.label: Land area, 2023
items.text: Territory to farm, power and protect.

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Rain and rivers renewed every year: power, irrigation and drinking water.

coverage.gap_text: Of the basic list of medicines is not available to Cubans.

guarantees.name: Food
guarantees.note: No FAO food insecurity survey is published for Cuba. WFP reports that the state ration covered only 46% of recommended daily energy in 2023

guarantees.name: Water
guarantees.note: On 3 November 2026, 2,681,770 Cubans, 28.4% of the population, had their piped water cut (INRH). 95.2% have basic water (WHO/UNICEF, 2024)

guarantees.name: Shelter
guarantees.note: Safely managed sanitation; 11% of city dwellers live in slums

guarantees.name: Energy
guarantees.note: At the evening peak on 10 November 2026 the grid could serve 970 of 2,900 MW of demand; the day before, supply was cut for all 24 hours. 96% cook with clean fuels (2024)

guarantees.name: Education
guarantees.note: 89.2% of young people complete lower secondary school

guarantees.name: Health
guarantees.note: Only 30% of the basic list of medicines is available (President of Cuba, August 2026). WHO service coverage index: 86 (2023)

guarantees.name: Livelihoods
guarantees.note: No poverty survey is published for Cuba. WFP reports that a household needed ten to eleven times the minimum monthly wage to buy the food it needs (2023)
